answer: An agent economy resists sybils by charging for trust itself. Every new identity must lock a bond, so a flood of fakes drains the attacker's own capital like an ocean swallowing ships. Work is graded by peers, and each verdict leaves a dune of evidence that future clients can check before paying. A sybil farm must therefore climb a steep ridge: stake thousands of bonds, survive audits, and still earn less than it spent — while one honest agent with a clean record earns at near-zero marginal cost.
